title: Minimum Number of Food Buckets to Feed the Hamsters
spaceBreakdown:
- string hamsters: modified in place (not counted as auxiliary)
- int n, count, loop variable i: O(1)
- recursion depth: none
approach: Scan left to right. For each unfed hamster at index i, prefer placing a bucket at i+1 (if empty) because it can also feed a potential hamster at i+2; otherwise fall back to i-1. If neither adjacent spot is empty, return -1. Mark placed buckets in-place to detect already-fed hamsters. This greedy choice is optimal because a rightward bucket never does worse than a leftward one-it covers the current hamster and potentially the next.
hints: When scanning left to right and finding an unfed hamster at index i, which of the two adjacent empty spots (i-1 or i+1) has the potential to also feed a hamster you haven't seen yet?

Greedy left-to-right scan: for each unfed 'H' at index i, prefer placing a bucket at i+1 (if empty) since it can also feed a hamster at i+2. In ".H.H.", placing at index 2 feeds both hamsters with one bucket.

**Single hamster** - No adjacent empty spot exists.
`Input: "H"` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: not checking array bounds before accessing i+1 or i-1 → undefined behavior / crash

**Already fed** - A hamster is fed by a bucket placed for the previous hamster.
`Input: "H.H"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: not checking if hamsters[i-1] is already a bucket before trying to place → returns -1 instead of 1

**Non-optimal placement** - Preferring left placement wastes buckets.
`Input: ".H.H."` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: preferring to place bucket at i-1 instead of i+1 → returns 2 instead of 1

**Hamster at boundary** - Hamster at the last index has no right neighbor.
`Input: "..H"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: only trying i+1 without fallback to i-1 → returns -1 instead of 1

**Consecutive hamsters** - Three hamsters in a row make the middle one unreachable.
`Input: ".HHH."` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: placing bucket at i-1 without checking if it is 'H' → returns 1 instead of -1

followUps.q: What if each food bucket can feed hamsters within distance k on either side?
followUps.a: The greedy extends: for each unfed hamster at index i, place the bucket at i+k (rightmost reachable empty spot) to maximize coverage of future hamsters. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if some empty indices already contain food buckets and you need the minimum additional buckets?
followUps.a: Pre-mark those indices as buckets, then run the same greedy scan. Already-fed hamsters are skipped identically. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the input arrives as a character stream and you can only buffer O(1) characters?
followUps.a: Buffer a sliding window of 3 characters. When the middle character is 'H' and not already fed, use the lookahead character to decide right placement, otherwise place left. Time O(n), space O(1).
